INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  Wednesday, December 11, 2024
  Open Session – 2:00 p.m.

  Web Sites:
  www.cityofinglewood.org/1680/Long-Term-Rentals

  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

The doors to the Council Chamber on the 9th Floor will open at 1:40 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful
that seating is limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the Rental Housing Board by sending them to the Rental Housing Board
Secretary at rentalhousingboard@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Rental
Housing Board prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the
meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number and/or subject matter.
Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 a.m. and
prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact
the Office of the Housing Protection Board at (310) 412-4330 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities
Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation
thereof. Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services
in order to observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation,
or service by contacting the Housing Protection Department by telephone at 310-412-4330, FAX at 310-412-
4276, One Manchester Boulevard, Suite 602, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to
rentalhousingboard@cityofinglewood.org no later than 48 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

  Call to Order

  Roll Call

  PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEMS

  Persons wishing to address the Inglewood Rental Housing Board on any item on the agenda may do so at
  this time.

  1.  Roll Call to ascertain if the Rental Housing Board Members have any conflict of interest with
  any item on the agenda.*
  Recommendation:
  1) Board Secretary to poll each Board Member to obtain a declaration.

  2.  Rental Housing Board Petition Process & Owner Petitions Module 3.

  Recommendation:
  1) Allow for Oral Presentation by RSG; and
  2) Questions and Answers.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS

  Persons wishing to address the Inglewood Rental Housing Board on any matter connected with the City
  of Inglewood Housing Protection Regulations not elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this
  time. Persons with complaints regarding departmental operations are requested to submit those complaints
  first to the Housing Protection Director for resolution.

  CHAIRPERSON AND BOARD MEMBER REMARKS

  ADJOURNMENT INGLEWOOD RENTAL HOUSING BOARD

  In the event that today’s meeting of the Inglewood Rental Housing Board is not held or is concluded prior
  to an agenda item being considered, the agenda item will automatically be continued to the next regularly
  scheduled Rental Housing Board meeting. If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability,
  or need translation services, please contact the Housing Protection Department at (310) 412-4330 or FAX
  (310) 412-4276, One Manchester Boulevard, Suite 602, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301. All
  requests for special accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to the day of the scheduled meeting.

   Rent Stabilization and Tenant Protects
  Fundamentals
  Policy  Description

  Rent Limits  Limits the amount landlords can increase rents each year – typically tied to the consumer price
  index (CPI) or may be fixed as a percentage of the current rent.

  Just Cause Eviction  Tenants can only be evicted for “just cause” reasons, typically categorized as at-fault and no-
  fault

  Relocation  Landlord is required to pay relocation assistance to the tenant when the reason for eviction is
  Assistance  no fault of the tenant (e.g. owner move-in, substantial rehabilitation)

  Vacancy Decontrol  Once a unit is vacated, landlords can “reset” rents to market rates without limitations (Costa
  Hawkins)

  Noticing  Landlords must serve proper notice before rent increases or evictions

 Fair Return Petition
  Policies and Procedures – Article 4

  Owner is requesting a rent increase of more than the published allowable increase to
  obtain a fair and reasonable return on their property.

 •  Formulaic Rent Increase
  •  5+ Units - 3% increase or Consumer Price Index (CPI) change whichever is greater.
  •  4 Units or less - 5% plus CPI or 10% whichever is lower.
 Fair Return Considerations

Law requires jurisdictions with rent increase limits to provide an
alternative process to ensure a fair return

  May result in a rent increase greater than the limit specified in the
  Ordinance (sometimes a lot higher!)

  Typically entails expensive, time-consuming process of reviewing
  income and expenses for specific calendar years

  Thorough review of all submitted income and expenses is crucial to
  ensure all expenses are allowable

   What is NOT a Capital Improvement?

  • Routine maintenance and repair
  • Examples: Pothole patching, street slurrying
  • Portable items, unless it is part of major rehabilitation
  • Examples: Pool furniture, landscaping equipment
  • Capital improvements for which the owner charges a fee to use
  • Examples: Coin-operated washing machines, parking spaces for which a fee is charged
  • Capital improvements for which the owner has been reimbursed through any insurance
  claim, litigation, or other right of indemnity

   Hearing Officer/Board Considerations

  • Confirmation that capital expenses used in the calculation should be allowed and are
  reasonable pursuant to the Ordinance
  • Determine the appropriate amortization period
  • Longer period = lower rent increase and higher total interest paid
  • Should align with useful life of capital improvements
  • Ordinance requires that the amortization period be long enough to keep the rent increase under a
  $100 per month increase
  • Decisions must be supported by findings based on substantial evidence submitted by the
